fact: Firestone requires artificial turf to be anchored at all edges and seams, and separated from other landscape areas by bender board, concrete curbing or a similar material that conceals the turf's edges.
quote: iv. Artificial turf shall be anchored at all edges and seams. … vi. Artificial turf shall be separated from other landscape areas by a bender board, concrete curbing or similar material to conceal edges of the turf.
source_label: Firestone Development Code 16.6.4.F.2.e.iv and e.vi (codified through Ord. No. 1072, Dec. 10, 2025)
notes: Read through the Municode API (api.municode.com CodesContent, jobId 488870 = Supplement 38, productId 18062) on 2026-09-25; the banner reads 'Codified through Ordinance No. 1072, adopted December 10, 2025.' The code does not say whether a turf edge tucked under sod or mulch counts as 'similar material' — hedge with 'ask Firestone Planning'.

fact: Firestone requires at least a 3-foot buffer of permeable surface with living and organic landscape material between the edge of artificial turf and any property line.
quote: A minimum of three (3) foot buffer comprised of permeable surfaces with living and organic landscape material shall be required between the edge of the artificial turf and any property line.
source_label: Firestone Development Code 16.6.4.F.2.b.iii (codified through Ord. No. 1072, Dec. 10, 2025)
notes: Read through the Municode API on 2026-09-25. Consequence for edging (our reading): a turf edge along a lot-line fence in Firestone meets a planted strip, not the fence.

fact: Firestone's maintenance standard says artificial turf areas may not show seam separations, uplifted surfaces, depressions or similar deterioration.
quote: Artificial turf areas shall not contain weeds, holes, tears, stains, discolorations, seam separations, uplifted surfaces, heat degradation, depressions, odors, excessive wear, or similar deformities and measures of deterioration.
source_label: Firestone Development Code 16.6.4.F.2.f.iii (codified through Ord. No. 1072, Dec. 10, 2025)
notes: Read through the Municode API on 2026-09-25.

fact: Firestone requires artificial turf placement, particularly under a tree's dripline, to avoid harming the tree when it is installed and over the tree's life.
quote: Artificial turf placement, particularly under the dripline of trees, shall avoid negative impacts to trees at the time of placement and during the lifespan of the tree.
source_label: Firestone Development Code 16.6.4.F.2.b.v (codified through Ord. No. 1072, Dec. 10, 2025)
notes: Read through the Municode API on 2026-09-25. Tree detail belongs to artificial-turf-around-trees; this page gives it one FAQ line.

fact: ForeverLawn's installation guidelines recommend perimeter boards on commercial jobs and allow either boards or spikes alone at the edge of a residential lawn; a pressure-treated 2x4 board stands on edge, the turf is fastened along its top, and pressure-treated lumber is chosen because it resists degradation.
quote: It is recommended to use boards around the perimeter in commercial applications. You can use boards or just secure the perimeter of the grass with spikes in a residential installation. If using the pressure treated lumber (typically a 2”x4”) it will be installed on edge, not laying flat. … Pressure treated perimeter boards are anchored in order to frame in the area. The synthetic grass is secured to the top edge of the boards. Pressure treated (2”x4”) boards are recommended as they resist degradation over time.
source_label: ForeverLawn, General Landscape Installation Guidelines (M1374 Rev. 05/19), PDF hosted by a ForeverLawn dealer
notes: Manufacturer's own document (form M1374), downloaded and read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25. The same guidelines call for crumb rubber infill, which Firestone bans; this page uses only the edge details.

fact: ForeverLawn sets the top of a perimeter board where the turf's backing will sit, typically 3/4 inch below the surrounding area and 3/4 to 1 inch below the edge of a sidewalk, and anchors boards that run along concrete with concrete screws or wedge anchor bolts.
quote: The top of the boards should be set to the level where you want the backing of the grass to be. With ForeverLawn synthetic grass, this is typically 3/4” below the surrounding area. For example, if going against a sidewalk, the top of the board should be 3/4”–1” below the edge of the sidewalk when installed. When the boards are installed adjacent to concrete (wall, house footer, sidewalk, driveway, etc.), use concrete screws or wedge anchor bolts to secure.
source_label: ForeverLawn, General Landscape Installation Guidelines (M1374 Rev. 05/19), Perimeter Board Installation
notes: One maker's figure for its own product; other turf differs with pile height.

fact: ForeverLawn screws perimeter boards to a fence or similar edge that can take screws, and holds a free-standing board with rebar, typically 1/2 inch and 18 to 24 inches long, driven through holes drilled about every 2 feet into the base beneath.
quote: If up against an edge (like a fence) that can be attached to, but isn’t concrete, just screw the boards in with deck screws. When the boards are not being attached to something, we call that free standing. Free standing boards should have holes center drilled through the board lengthwise (as the board will be standing on the 2” edge). These holes are typically every 2’ on center. Rebar should then be pounded through the hole into the base beneath. … Rebar–typically 1/2” that are 18”–24” in length if using rebar to secure board.
source_label: ForeverLawn, General Landscape Installation Guidelines (M1374 Rev. 05/19), Critical Supplies and Perimeter Board Installation

fact: Without boards, ForeverLawn tucks the turf edge under a soft edge such as sod or a mulch bed, pulling the neighboring material back and returning it once the edge is secured, and fills stone, mulch or grass up to a free-standing edge without going above the yard's finish grade.
quote: When the grass edge terminates along a soft or exposed edge (existing sod or mulch bed) the existing material should be pulled back so that the synthetic grass dives beneath it. The material from the yard can then be brought back into place after the edges are secured creating a seamless transition from artificial to natural surfacing. … On free standing edges, the material on the other side of the ForeverLawn synthetic grass (natural grass, stone, mulch, etc.) can now be filled up to the wrapped edge not exceeding the finish grade of the yard.
source_label: ForeverLawn, General Landscape Installation Guidelines (M1374 Rev. 05/19), Spike Option and Clean Up

fact: Against a wall or other hard edge, ForeverLawn marks the turf on its back and cuts it so it stops millimeters short of the edge.
quote: When cutting to an edge, the grass should be marked and cut so the grass comes just short (we’re talking millimeters) of the wall.
source_label: ForeverLawn, General Landscape Installation Guidelines (M1374 Rev. 05/19), Trimming the Grass

fact: SYNLawn's DIY installation guidelines set the compacted base 1 to 1.5 inches below a neighboring concrete slab or walkway, depending on the turf's pile height and the project's design.
quote: Note: When installing next to a concrete slab or walkway the compacted base should be 1” to 1.5” below the surrounding concrete. This depends on pile height of turf and project design.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (PDF hosted by Lowe's), Installing the Base
notes: Manufacturer's DIY guide, downloaded and read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25.

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, a turf distributor, calls bender board an important step because it gives a clean line and separates planting beds from turf, and treats tucking the turf's edge against hardscape or an edging border with a wonder bar as an optional step.
quote: Install Bender Board—the installation of the bender board is an important step as it provides a clean line and separation for the plants or bed and turf areas. … Tucking the turf involves hiding the edges of the turf against any hardscape or edging border by using a metal bar called a wonder bar. The side edges of the turf give it a good clean plush look. This is an optional step and can be performed based on the needs of the project.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, How To Install Artificial Grass (step-by-step guide)

fact: Greenline Artificial Grass's installation guide uses a 2x4 bender board for straight runs and a 1x2 for curves, in synthetic or pressure-treated wood, around the perimeter to frame the turf and protect it from soil and debris.
quote: Use a 2×4 (straight line installation) or 1×2 (curve line installation) of synthetic or pressure treated wood bender board around the perimeter of turf area to frame and protect the turf from soil and debris.
source_label: Greenline Artificial Grass, Synthetic Grass Installation Guide

fact: Sure-loc, an aluminum edging maker, says its long grooved stakes help reduce frost heaving, sells them 12 or 18 inches long, and puts pockets in its edging that take a stake at a 45-degree angle to keep the edging in the ground when temperature changes shift the soil.
quote: Long and wide grooved stakes help reduce the effects of frost heaving. … Available in 12” or 18” lengths in all colors and sizes. Anti Frost Heave Technology. Stake pockets in edging accept a stake at a 45 degree angle to help keep the edging in the ground when temperature changes cause ground shifting.
source_label: Sure-loc Edging, Aluminum Edging (manufacturer product page)
notes: A maker's own product description. The page also disparages steel edging; this page does not repeat that comparison.

fact: Sure-loc's installation instructions set the top of its edging no more than 1/2 inch above finish grade beside turf, with the grade compacted next to the edging to avoid settling.
quote: Top of edging to be no more than 1/2" (12.7mm) above finish grade … Compact grade adjacent to edging to avoid settling
source_label: Sure-loc Brand Aluminum Landscape Edging, Installation Instructions (PDF)
notes: Callouts on the installation drawing, which shows the edging beside turf (natural lawn in the drawing).

fact: K-State Research and Extension says edging keeps grass out of beds and pathway materials out of gardens and lawns, and a raised edge keeps soil and mulch from washing out of beds in heavy rain.
quote: From a practical standpoint, edging keeps grass from invading shrub or garden areas. It keeps pathway materials out of gardens and lawns. From a cost and maintenance standpoint, a raised edging prevents erosion by keeping soil and mulch from washing out of beds during heavy rains.
source_label: Johnson County K-State Research and Extension, All About Edging (Extension Master Gardeners, Rev. 2022)
notes: Kansas extension fact sheet on garden edging generally, not turf; used for how edge materials behave.

fact: K-State Research and Extension's simplest lawn edge is a trench 4 to 6 inches deep and wide, angled toward the bed so grass roots cannot easily cross, re-cut once or twice a season.
quote: Using an edger or a sharp flat spade, make a trench or V-shaped ditch 4 to 6 inches deep and wide, angling towards the bed so that grass roots cannot easily cross. The only maintenance required is to re-cut the edge once or twice during the growing season before the invasion of grass or plants becomes a nuisance.
source_label: Johnson County K-State Research and Extension, All About Edging (Rev. 2022), Cut-edge or Trench Edging

fact: K-State Research and Extension says bricks or pavers set flush with the ground control spreading grasses and make a mowing strip that removes the need for a trimmer, cement curbing also makes a mowing strip but must be professionally installed and is permanent, and loose stone lets spreading grasses into its gaps unless it is mortared.
quote: This type of edge controls spreading grasses and unruly plants, defines an area and reduces maintenance. … When installed flush with the ground, they provide a mowing strip, thus eliminating the need for using a weed trimmer. … Like brick and pavers, cement curbing is attractive and durable. However, it must be professionally installed. Cement also provides a mowing strip, but its permanence does not allow for easy expansion of the gardens in the future. … unless the stones are mortared together, spreading turf grasses will quickly find their way into nooks and crannies.
source_label: Johnson County K-State Research and Extension, All About Edging (Rev. 2022), Bricks and pavers; Cement curbing; Gathered stone
notes: The source's own sentence ranking bricks and pavers is not quoted in copy.

fact: K-State Research and Extension says wood edging will eventually rot, metal and hard plastic strips give an underground barrier, painted metal delays rust, and frost may heave or crack plastic edging over time while grass can grow over it.
quote: It will last for many years but will eventually rot. … Metal and hard plastic polyvinyl edging strips are reasonably priced and provide an underground barrier, but are lacking in aesthetics and should be installed so that only the top shows. … Using painted metal will help to delay the onset of rust. … Frost may cause heaving or cracking over time. Ground covers and grass can often grow over them, defeating their purpose.
source_label: Johnson County K-State Research and Extension, All About Edging (Rev. 2022), Wood; Metal and hard plastic polyvinyl
notes: The frost sentence closes the paragraph on plastic strips and short hard-plastic sections.

fact: CSU Extension says Kentucky bluegrass is sod-forming with underground rhizomes and will invade flower and vegetable gardens, and that buffalograss's aggressive stolons may invade flower beds and neighboring lawns.
quote: Sod-forming (has underground rhizomes) … Will invade flower and vegetable gardens … Sod-former (aggressive stolons) … Aggressive stolons may invade flower beds, neighboring lawns.
source_label: CSU Extension, CMG GardenNotes #561, Turfgrass Species Selection Guidelines
notes: The first two phrases are from the Kentucky bluegrass list, the last two from buffalograss.

fact: Penn State Extension says Kentucky bluegrass rhizomes grow beneath the soil surface for a short distance and then turn up to form new shoots.
quote: Rhizomes grow below ground for a short distance, then rise to the soil surface to form new shoots. … Rhizomes of Kentucky bluegrass and creeping red fescue grow beneath the soil surface and then turn up towards the soil surface to form new shoots.
source_label: Penn State Extension, The Cool-Season Turfgrasses: Basic Structures, Growth and Development (Peter Landschoot, updated Sept. 19, 2025)

fact: The Concrete Masonry & Hardscapes Association says pavers need an edge restraint to hold them tightly together, that flat metal or plastic landscape edging around beds is not an acceptable paver restraint, that soil backfill never is, and that timber warps and eventually rots.
quote: Edge restraints are an essential component of interlocking concrete pavements. Restraints hold the pavers tightly together, enabling consistent interlock of the units across the entire pavement. … Soil backfill is never a suitable edge restraint … Flat metal or plastic landscape edging used around plantings and flower beds is not an acceptable restraint for interlocking concrete pavements. They do not provide enough lateral support to hold the pavers tightly together and maintain interlock. Timber is not recommended for an edge restraint because it warps and eventually rots.
source_label: Concrete Masonry & Hardscapes Association, PAV-TEC-003-22 Edge Restraints for Interlocking Concrete Pavements (revised 2022)
notes: CMHA succeeded the Interlocking Concrete Pavement Institute; this is the former ICPI Tech Spec 3.

fact: CMHA's rule of thumb is that the base should run past a paver edge restraint at least as far as the base is thick, which adds stability especially in soils subject to heaving, and edge restraints are designed to stay put through freeze-thaw cycles.
quote: Edge restraints are designed to remain stationary while receiving impacts during installation, from vehicles and from freeze-thaw cycles. … The rule of thumb is the base should extend beyond the restraint at least the same dimension as the thickness of the base material. For example, a 6 in. (150 mm) thick base should extend at least 6 in. (150 mm) beyond the spikes in the restraints. This contributes stability to the restraint especially in soils subject to heaving.
source_label: Concrete Masonry & Hardscapes Association, PAV-TEC-003-22 Edge Restraints for Interlocking Concrete Pavements (revised 2022)

fact: Kinston at Centerra's design guidelines in Loveland allow planting-bed edges that are spaded or aluminum, and send any other landscape edging material to the Design Review Board for approval.
quote: EDGING MATERIALS Shrub bed edges may be spaded or may use aluminum edging materials. Other landscape edging materials may be used with the review and approval by the DRB.
source_label: Kinston at Centerra, Home Builder Design Guidelines, November 2025 (McWhinney), Landscape section
notes: Builder design guidelines for the Kinston neighborhood; changes by owners go through its review board. Downloaded (23.9 MB PDF) and read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25.

fact: Heron Lakes' design rules in Berthoud recommend concrete edging where a lot's landscaping meets the common-area landscaping, and allow non-irrigated artificial turf as part of xeriscape.
quote: Individual site landscaping should be coordinated with existing common area landscaping. Concrete edging is recommended in these areas. … Xeriscape is allowed within Heron Lakes, including non-irrigated artificial turf.
source_label: Berthoud-Heritage Metropolitan District, Heron Lakes Residential Improvement Rules and Regulations (amended June 1, 2026), Secs. 4.4 and 4.8(a)
notes: Downloaded and read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25.

fact: In Timnath's Kitchel Lake neighborhood, Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1 requires landscaping plans approved by its architectural control committee before installation, showing the types and locations of edging among other features.
quote: Landscaping plans must be approved by the ACC prior to installation. … Plans shall depict types and locations of: fencing, decks, playing areas, sod, seeded areas, edging, retaining walls, rock areas, sprinkler systems, flower beds/gardens, other planting beds, mulch areas, landscape lighting and any other components of the proposed plan.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Sec. 37.A
notes: Downloaded and read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25.
